title.narrative: Addressing Hydro-climatic Risks and Building Water Resilience in Small Island Development States (Be-Resilient SIDS)

description.narrative: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) face accelerating hydro-climatic risks due to climate change, including rising temperatures, tropical cyclones, storm surges, droughts, changing precipitation patterns, sea level rise, coral bleaching, and invasive species. These factors impact natural systems and human livelihoods, with millions living in vulnerable areas. Data from the International Disaster Database (EM-DAT) reveals significant impacts from floods, droughts, and storms in Caribbean and African SIDS, affecting 8,934,481 individuals and resulting in 583 deaths from 2020 to May 2024. Small atoll islands see an 11-36% decline in groundwater due to sea level rise. Droughts increase water scarcity, affecting agriculture and population growth. Gaps in resilience-building, long-term adaptation planning, and climate finance hinder effective adaptation. Limited climate and hydrological data complicate decision-making and adaptation efforts. The project aims to enhance climate-resilient water resource management, aligning with the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP IX 2022-2029) and international agendas. It will improve local stakeholders' knowledge, strengthen hydro-climatic monitoring and early warning, and support policy frameworks for better adaptation to climate change. UNESCO sites will serve as testing grounds for climate-resilient water management strategies.
